item.title: Right-wing candidate pulls ahead in first round of Colombia's presidential vote
item.description: Tough-on-crime outsider Aberaldo de la Espriella took the lead in Colombia's presidential race on Sunday night, setting up a runoff with Iván Cepeda, an ally of outgoing President Gustavo Petro.

item.title: U.S. bombs Iranian military sites and Kuwait is hit by drone and missile fire
item.description: The U.S. military says it bombed Iranian radar and drone control sites in Iran after Tehran shot down an American MQ-1 Predator drone this weekend. Kuwait said its air defenses opened fire on Monday.

item.title: Iran attacks damage 20 US military sites since start of war, satellite images show
item.description: Analysts told BBC Verify that Tehran's strikes were more extensive than publicly acknowledged.

item.title: Iran and US report new wave of air strikes in Gulf
item.description: Washington and Tehran targeted each other's military facilities around the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Athlete forced to travel 800 miles for meeting says £149k tribunal win could help thousands
item.description: Beth Littlewood says driving from Germany for a meeting with her no-show boss was the "final straw".

item.title: 'Don't be too kind': Stories from the maternity unit where mums were failed
item.description: BBC Panorama has seen documents and spoken to former midwives from Nottingham University Hospitals NHS Trust.

item.title: Colombia presidential runoff pits leftist senator against pro-Trump rival
item.description: Left-wing senator Iván Cepeda will face Trump admirer Abelardo de la Espriella at the final ballot on 21 June.

item.title: Trump seeking edits to US-Iran deal, US media report
item.description: The requested changes are related to the Strait of Hormuz and the removal of highly enriched uranium, according to US media.

item.title: How aid cuts are hampering the frontline response to the Ebola crisis
item.description: Aid workers in Uganda are watching the Ebola crisis unfold in the neighboring Democratic Republic of Congo. They're doing what they can to prepare for an uptick in cases, but foreign aid cuts aren't helping.
